openAPIV3Schema.description: Virtual IP address of the Kubernetes API. It moves between the control-plane nodes, so it is an unused address on the nodes' network and outside the range in network.addresses.

addresses.description: Addresses the nodes take theirs from, as ranges (10.0.0.10-10.0.0.20), networks in CIDR notation or single addresses.

bridge.description: Proxmox VE bridge the nodes connect to.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Proxmox VE storage for the nodes' disks and the cluster's persistent volumes.
Proxmox VE nodes the cluster's VMs may run on; every node when unset. New VMs go to those of them that are online.

Whether Proxmox VE HA keeps the control-plane VMs on separate nodes and restarts them on another node when theirs fails. It takes effect where Kubehenge's administrator has enabled Proxmox VE HA and the cluster's disks are on shared storage.
The Proxmox VE CSI plugin, which every cluster runs for its persistent volumes.

datastoreAllocate.description: Run the plugin's newest release, which needs Datastore.Allocate on the cluster's storage, and give the cluster's Proxmox VE token Datastore.Allocate there: it may then delete any volume on that storage and change the storage's definition. Only where Kubehenge's administrator lets clusters choose it, and on a storage that neither the management cluster, its templates nor another cluster uses. Off, the cluster runs the plugin's last release that needs no more than Datastore.AllocateSpace.

volumeSnapshots.description: Take VolumeSnapshots of the cluster's persistent volumes, restore them and clone volumes. A proxy beside the plugin makes each copy with the cluster's own Proxmox VE token, as an unused disk of one of the cluster's holder VMs, and only of the cluster's own volumes. Only on storage local to each node (ZFS, LVM, LVM-thin, directory or btrfs), and a copy stays on its volume's node. Off, the snapshot components go, and the plugin reaches Proxmox VE directly again once no copy is left.

openAPIV3Schema.description: The Proxmox VE cloud controller manager, which every cluster runs for its nodes.

haGroups.description: Give the cluster's Proxmox VE token Sys.Audit on /, unpropagated, so that the cloud controller manager labels each node group.topology.proxmox.sinextra.dev/<group> for each Proxmox VE HA group, or node-affinity HA rule, its Proxmox VE node is in. The token may then also read the rest of the Proxmox VE cluster's own configuration (firewall, backup jobs, HA, corosync), but nothing of its guests, storages or nodes. On by default where Kubehenge's administrator lets clusters hold it, and only there.

diskGiB.description: Size of the boot disk. A disk only grows, so it is never below the template's.
Size of the boot disk. A disk only grows, so it is never below the template's.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Headlamp, a web interface for the cluster. Users sign in with their own token or through OIDC, and Headlamp itself has no rights in the cluster, unless access is view. Reached through Kubehenge's interface, or at hostname when one is set.

access.description: token: everyone signs in with their own token or through OIDC. view: Headlamp's own service account is bound to the view ClusterRole and Headlamp uses it for everyone, so whoever reaches Headlamp sees the cluster read-only without signing in (no Secrets), and a token given to it is not used.

hostname.description: Also serve Headlamp at this name through the cluster's ingress controller.

tlsSecret.description: Secret in the headlamp namespace holding the certificate for hostname. When unset, the certificates add-on's while it is on, else the ingress controller's own default.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana with the kube-prometheus-stack dashboards and alerts, scraping every node and control-plane component over verified, authenticated TLS. Installs cert-manager too. Grafana's admin password is in the kube-prometheus-stack-grafana Secret in the monitoring namespace.

hostname.description: Serve Grafana at this name through the cluster's ingress controller.

tlsSecret.description: Secret in the monitoring namespace holding the certificate for hostname. When unset, the certificates add-on's while it is on, else the ingress controller's own default.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Loki, keeping the cluster's logs and its events on a volume of their own, read in monitoring's Grafana, which they need, and Grafana Alloy collecting them. Only Alloy may push to Loki and only Grafana read it, each by its client certificate, besides users whose RBAC allows them the Loki paths. Switched off, the volume stays.

collector.description: node runs Alloy on every node, reading the files the kubelet writes, the node's journal and on the control planes the API server's audit log, so it catches pods gone again within seconds; it reads host paths as root without capabilities, from the privileged logging-node namespace. api runs one Alloy without anything of the host, reading the pods' logs through the Kubernetes API: lighter, but without journals or audit log, and it can miss pods that live only seconds.

sizeGiB.description: Loki's volume, in GiB, which has to hold the retention's worth of logs: Loki takes no lines while it is full. It only grows.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: Loki's volume only grows.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Velero backing up the cluster's resources and volumes on a schedule to one of the S3 targets an administrator set, under a prefix of the cluster's own, and restoring them. What it stores is encrypted with keys of the cluster's own, which Kubehenge keeps beside the Cluster in the <cluster>-backup-keys Secret: the objects by the store (SSE-C), the volumes' data by Kopia. kube-system, which holds the cluster's Proxmox VE token, and the add-ons' namespaces are left out. Velero reads every volume as root from the privileged velero namespace. Switched off, Velero goes and the backups stay in the target.

existingSecret.description: Secret in the workload cluster's velero namespace with the store's keys as Velero's credentials file, under the key cloud, which never passes through the management cluster; unset, the credential typed into the interface for the cluster. The one for every cluster never goes into a cluster.

readFrom.description: Clusters of the same namespace, backing up to the same target, whose backups this one may restore. Velero gets a read-only location named cluster-<name> for each, with that cluster's SSE-C key, so whoever is cluster-admin here can read what those backups hold. The volumes' data comes back only when this cluster's keys were made while it read that cluster's backups, as it then shares that cluster's Kopia password.

retentionDays.description: Days each backup is kept before Velero deletes it from the target.

schedule.description: When to back up, as a cron expression of five fields or a descriptor such as @weekly.

target.description: The administrator's target to back up to, by name.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone the schedule is read in, such as Europe/Berlin.

volumes.description: all backs up every volume of every pod but emptyDir ones; annotated only the volumes a pod names in its backup.velero.io/backup-volumes annotation.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: Backups need a target.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Snapshots of the cluster's etcd, which holds every object of the cluster but its volumes' data, on a schedule to one of the S3 targets an administrator set, beside the cluster's Velero backups in an etcd folder of its own. Kubehenge's controller takes each snapshot through the cluster's API server with a client certificate it signs for itself, encrypts it with age to a key of the cluster's own in the <cluster>-backup-keys Secret, and stores it with the credential typed into the interface for the cluster, or else the one for every cluster; no key or credential enters the cluster. Restoring one brings back the cluster's objects as they were, for a cluster that lost its etcd quorum or had its objects deleted or damaged.

distributionUpload.description: RKE2 and k3s only: have the cluster's servers also take snapshots themselves on the same schedule, read in UTC, and upload them to the target's <distribution>-etcd folder of the cluster, keeping as many, as etcd holds them and not encrypted by Kubehenge. For it the controller puts the target and the cluster's own access key, never the one for every cluster, into the Secret kubehenge-etcd-s3 in the cluster's kube-system, where whoever may read Secrets there reads the key and with it everything the key reaches in the target. Switching it, or changing the schedule or keep while it is on, replaces the control-plane machines.

keep.description: How many snapshots to keep; the oldest beyond are deleted from the target.

schedule.description: When to take a snapshot, as a cron expression of five fields or a descriptor such as @daily.

target.description: The administrator's target to store the snapshots in, by name.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone the schedule is read in, such as Europe/Berlin.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: etcd snapshots need a target.
The distribution's own upload takes the target, schedule and keep of etcd snapshots, which are off.

openAPIV3Schema.description: The Pod Security Standard the cluster's pods are held to, by Kubernetes' Pod Security Admission, by Kyverno, or by both. The namespaces of the components that need the host (kube-system, Calico's, node-exporter's, Alloy's node collectors', Velero's, Istio's node agents', MetalLB's, Rancher's and its agents') are exempt from Pod Security Admission in every cluster, and from Kyverno where the cluster runs them.

admission.description: The level Pod Security Admission enforces in every namespace that labels none of its own. Pods short of restricted are warned about and audited at every level. Changing it replaces the control-plane machines.

kyverno.description: The level Kyverno's Pod Security Standards policies enforce, in every namespace and whatever its labels say, with a policy report of what falls short; off leaves Kyverno out of the cluster.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Istio in ambient mode: a namespace labelled istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient has its pods' traffic carried over mutual TLS between them, with their workload identities, and no sidecars. Switching it off first takes every namespace and pod out of the mesh.

Cilium Cluster Mesh, for a cluster that runs Cilium: its pods reach those of the clusters it is linked with, by address and through global services, and Cilium's network policies can select them. Two clusters of one namespace are linked while both are on and list each other, with pod ranges apart; each then reads the other's pod names, labels and identities.

peers.description: The clusters of this namespace to link with.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Addresses for the cluster's Services of type LoadBalancer, from a range on the nodes' network. One node at a time answers for each address, and another takes over when it fails. Without it, kubeadm and RKE2 give such Services no address, and k3s's servicelb answers for them on every node's own address.

addresses.description: Addresses the Services take theirs from, as ranges (10.0.0.30-10.0.0.40), networks in CIDR notation or single addresses: unused addresses on the nodes' network, apart from network.addresses, the control-plane endpoint, the gateway, the network's own and broadcast addresses and other clusters' addresses there. Services outside a changed range take new addresses from it.

implementation.description: MetalLB, or kube-vip, which also holds the cluster's API address. Switching replaces the one with the other; Services keep their addresses where the new one can, and take new ones from the range otherwise.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: A load balancer needs addresses.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Rancher. One cluster installs it, and Kubehenge registers every other cluster with it unless that cluster sets register to false; a cluster leaves Rancher before it is deleted.

hostname.description: Name Rancher is reached at, by people and by every registered cluster's agent; it resolves to this cluster's ingress controller, such as its control-plane virtual IP.

install.description: Install Rancher into this cluster. Kubernetes stays within the versions the installed Rancher release runs on.

register.description: Register this cluster with the Rancher Kubehenge installed.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: Rancher needs a hostname.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Certificates from cert-manager for the cluster's Ingresses, routes and Gateways. With DNS-01 or the cluster's CA, a certificate for domain and every name one label beneath it is the one Traefik serves wherever no other is asked for, and Traefik's Gateway listens for HTTPS with it. An Ingress annotated cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: kubehenge-ingress, or kubernetes.io/tls-acme: "true", gets its own certificate from the same issuer. Installs cert-manager too.

caBundle.description: PEM of the CA that signed the ACME server's own certificate, for a server whose certificate the system's CAs do not vouch for.

email.description: The ACME account's contact, told of certificates about to expire.

server.description: The ACME server's directory; Let's Encrypt's when unset.

staging.description: Let's Encrypt's staging directory, whose certificates no browser trusts.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: Staging is Let's Encrypt's own directory; it cannot go with another server.

existingSecret.description: A Secret in the workload cluster's cert-manager namespace holding the credential under the key token; Akamai's under clientToken, clientSecret and accessToken.

nameservers.description: The DNS servers (host:port) cert-manager checks the challenge's record with, for a domain whose answers inside the cluster differ from the public ones.

provider.description: The DNS provider whose API sets the challenge's record. Its credential is the one stored for the cluster in the interface, unless existingSecret or sharedCredential says otherwise: Cloudflare's or DigitalOcean's API token, Route 53's secret access key, the Azure service principal's client secret, the Google service account's JSON key, the TSIG secret, or the ACME-DNS account's JSON.

nameserver.description: The DNS server (host:port) that takes the dynamic update.

sharedCredential.description: Take the DNS-01 credential an administrator stored for every cluster rather than one of the cluster's own.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: The credential comes from an existing Secret or from the one shared by every cluster, not both.
Akamai's three secrets come only from an existing Secret.
Akamai needs its service consumer domain.
Route 53 needs its region and access key ID.
Azure DNS needs its subscription, resource group, tenant and client IDs.
Google Cloud DNS needs its project.
RFC 2136 needs its nameserver and TSIG key name.
ACME-DNS needs its host.

domain.description: The domain of the default certificate, which covers it and *.domain. The cluster's CA signs names in it alone, and a new domain makes a new CA.

issuer.description: Where certificates come from: an ACME server such as Let's Encrypt, proving the names through the DNS provider's API (acme-dns01) or over HTTP on port 80 (acme-http01, which gives no default certificate), or a CA of the cluster's own (ca), whose certificate the interface hands out for clients to trust.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: DNS-01 and the cluster's CA need a domain.
DNS-01 needs a DNS provider.

openAPIV3Schema.description: GitOps: Argo CD or Flux keeps the cluster in step with a directory of a Git repository, applying what it holds and removing what goes from it. Switching it off, or to the other engine, removes the engine and leaves what it deployed running.

admins.description: Groups of the cluster's first OIDC provider that administer Argo CD; nobody else has any rights in it. Flux's web interface acts as the signed-in user, with the cluster's own RBAC.

auth.description: How the engine reads the repository: none for a public one over HTTPS; deployKey, a key pair Kubehenge makes, whose public half you add to the repository as a read-only deploy key; token, a user name and token over HTTPS, stored as the cluster's gitops credential; or existingSecret, a Secret of your own in the engine's namespace.

engine.description: Argo CD, with a web interface that signs in through the cluster's first OIDC provider, or Flux, installed by the Flux Operator, whose web interface is optional.

existingSecret.description: With auth existingSecret: for Flux, a Secret in flux-system as a GitRepository's secretRef takes it (identity and known_hosts, or username and password); for Argo CD, a repository Secret in argocd labelled argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=repository for this URL.

hostname.description: Serve the engine's web interface at this name through the cluster's ingress controller.

knownHosts.description: The SSH host keys of the repository's server, as known_hosts lines (ssh-keygen -F or the forge's published keys), at least one for its host. Required for a repository reached over ssh://, but Flux's with credentials from a Secret of your own, which carries them: Kubehenge never reads them from the network.

path.description: The directory synced, with plain manifests or a kustomization; the repository's root by default.

revision.description: A branch, or a full ref such as refs/tags/v1.

url.description: The repository, as https://host/path or ssh://user@host[:port]/path; ssh:// is read with a deploy key or a Secret of your own.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: A token goes into the cluster's gitops credential, not into the URL.
The path stays inside the repository.

signIn.description: How the web interface signs in through the cluster's first OIDC provider: as that provider's client unless clientID names another, without a client secret, using PKCE, unless one is given. Argo CD's local admin stays disabled.

clientSecret.description: none for a public client; stored, the cluster's oidc-client credential; or existingSecret, a Secret of your own in the engine's namespace with the key clientSecret, labelled app.kubernetes.io/part-of=argocd for Argo CD.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: A client secret from a Secret of your own needs the Secret's name.

tlsSecret.description: Secret in the engine's namespace holding the certificate for hostname. When unset, the certificates add-on's while it is on, else the ingress controller's own default.

ui.description: Flux's web interface, at hostname: it shows every Flux object and the workloads they deployed, and lets those signed in reconcile, suspend and resume them, with the rights the cluster's RBAC gives them. It signs in with a client secret.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: GitOps needs a repository.
A deploy key reads the repository over ssh://.
A repository reached over ssh:// needs its host's keys in knownHosts.
Without a key, the repository is read over https://.
Credentials from a Secret of your own need the Secret's name.
The web interface is Flux's, and needs a hostname.
Flux's web interface signs in with a client secret.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Upgrade Kubernetes automatically, and move the nodes to new builds of their VM template, inside a maintenance window. Kubehenge's controller takes the newest release the mode allows, one minor version at a time and never past the distribution's stable channel, and starts only when the cluster is healthy and no rollout is running. A started rollout finishes even if the window ends first.

mode.description: patch stays on the cluster's minor version; minor also moves to the next one.

nodeImages.description: Replace the nodes inside the window with clones of the newest build of their VM template, which carries their node OS's updates, once that build is a day old, whatever mode says. Nodes are replaced one at a time, as in an upgrade. Talos nodes take their updates by upgrading Talos instead.

start.description: When the window opens, as HH:MM.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of start, such as Europe/Berlin.

weekdays.description: Days of the week the window opens on; with monthDays, a day listed in either counts. Every day when both are empty.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Operating system of the nodes, a family and one of its releases, as Kubehenge builds its VM templates: the family's own signed packages and only those a node needs, SELinux enforcing with the distribution's policy, and for AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux an image-mode system whose /usr is read-only. Changing it replaces every node with a clone of the new node OS's template, one at a time as in an upgrade; that template has to be built first.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a release of the family Kubehenge builds templates of: almalinux-10, rocky-10

openAPIV3Schema.description: How the cluster autoscaler scales the cluster's autoscaled pools: those whose topology entry carries cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-api-autoscaler-node-group-min-size and -max-size and no replicas. Kubehenge's controller runs it while the cluster has such a pool.

expander.description: Which pool grows when several could take the waiting pods.

placement.description: Where the autoscaler runs. management keeps it in the management cluster, and the cluster holds no credential of the management cluster. workload runs it on the cluster's control planes, sparing the management cluster its memory, and puts a management-cluster token inside the cluster that can read every cluster's machines in its namespace; the admission policy still lets it scale only this cluster's pools.

scaleDownDelayAfterAddMinutes.description: How long after a scale-up the autoscaler waits before it removes any node.

scaleDownUnneededMinutes.description: How long a node stays unneeded before the autoscaler removes it.

openAPIV3Schema.description: OpenID Connect providers whose ID tokens the API server accepts, besides certificates and ServiceAccount tokens. A token's audience has to be the provider's clientID. Headlamp and kubectl sign in with the first one; tokens keep working beside it.

certificateAuthority.description: PEM CA of the provider's certificate, when the system's do not cover it.

clientID.description: The client sign-in tools use; tokens must be issued to it.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: Kubernetes keeps system: for its own users and groups.

issuerURL.description: The provider's issuer, exactly as its tokens name it.

scopes.description: Scopes sign-in tools ask for besides openid; the API server does not read them.

usernamePrefix.description: Put before every user name, so none can pass for a user of another kind.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: Kubernetes keeps system: for its own users and groups.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Harden the cluster to the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark beyond what every cluster gets: Pod Security Admission enforces restricted outside the exempt namespaces, every container runs under the runtime's default seccomp profile unless it asks for another, and exec, attach and port-forward sessions end after five idle minutes. RKE2 also runs its own CIS profile, under which pods in kube-system, kube-public and default take connections only from their own namespace, DNS and a few of RKE2's own services aside. May be switched on after creation, which replaces every node, and never off again.

openAPIV3Schema.description: Labels and taints the nodes of the worker pools register with, kept when a node is replaced. A worker pool may set its own, which replaces these. Changing them replaces the pool's nodes, one at a time.
